summary: The pane-tint change does what it was meant to do, and nothing else moved. In the side-on PY/Y/J/F views the day panes now sit a little above the white lining instead of below it. ra_yWin pane G p50 is 238 -> 248 against lining 241; the y_47300 panes are 251 against wall 237. The cool cast is roughly halved (R-B -12 -> -8; the photos are about -1). Cloud texture is kept: nothing clips (0 % of pixels at 254+ in every view) and high-pass detail is unchanged or slightly higher (ra_yWin 1.73 -> 1.61, s09 4.47 -> 4.84, ra_pyWin 5.78 -> 6.54). So the panes read as bright, near-white glass, not as flat blown cards. They are still not the pure #fff glare of c_27316 (G 255, saturation 1.3), but that is exposure, which belongs to lighting. q12 is not worse: the scene mean is up only 3 levels (115/123/134 -> 118/126/136), the wing and sky keep their contrast (G p95 193 -> 201, max unchanged at 238-239), and there is no washout. The before/after diffs show changes only on glass pixels (plus cloud motion). q15, s05 and ra_door2floor are pixel-identical, so there is no regression. This is a small, real gain in window-glass fidelity. It is not enough to lift the area above 8.5, because the carried low items (door viewing window, pleat contrast, vinyl speckle, sidewall weave, tub-floor card, grille pitch, F carpet grain) are untouched.
